newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies at day's highs.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies at day's highs.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mixed after fund rolling and profit taking offset support from Thursday's firm cash hog prices, traders said. Pork bellies closed at the day's highs on strong technicals and support from firm cash belly prices.

Hog futures finished 0.300 cent a lb higher to 0.150 lower with February up most and December off 0.100 at 56.700 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.200 to 0.500 cent higher with February up 1.050 at 72.900 cents, the highest level since mid-October.
Profit taking linked to the premium futures hold to cash values added to fund rolling and offset the current firm tone to cash hog and pork prices, traders said.

Heavier-than-expected hog weights also prompted some of the nervous long liquidation in December. Much of the fund rolling, selling of December and buying of February was the "Goldman roll". However, other commission houses and commercials were buying December and selling February based on strong cash ideas into early next year, traders said.
"Expansion of the hog herd is on and this takes gilts off the top of the marketings," one trader said.
Refco sold December and bought February. Rand Financials and Stone Traders were on the opposite side, sources said.

In live hog options, volatility was soft in December on the time decay, which is the shrinking of the premium leading up to expiration. Merrill Lynch bought October 64 calls late. Scattered buying of December 54 and 56 puts early was noted, pit sources added.
Pork bellies remained strong and moved up to day's highs at the close on strong technical and cash support. LIT division of First Options was a notable buyer, traders said.

Charts pointed higher for belly futures and prices finished just under the level that would bring in short covering by funds. A close above 73.200 cents, basis February, would spark the covering, one chartist said.

Fundamental support was again evident in view of recent lighter-than-expected storings. Futures need to widen their premium to cash to encourage larger storings for next year's peak demand season, traders said.
"We have to continue lifting the (futures) price until storings increase," one trader said.
